1#א: Beriah — and all these are not nullified only d'rabbanan, but from the Torah they are nullified; and on this Peleti in Tosafot's words and commentators, and I raised that it is only d'rabbanan.
1#ב: And an egg that has an embryo in it — see Peleti that Rashba disagrees; and where there is further room to be lenient, one may combine and say it is not called beriah.
1#ג: Embryo — but if there is blood in it, all agree it is not beriah; and see Peleti; and know that the Mechaber's intent in his statement "an egg that has an embryo in it" is the opposite of what was in the egg — meaning there was an embryo in the egg and they removed it and it mixed with other embryos and is not recognizable — it teaches that this embryo that was in the egg is forbidden from the beginning of its creation and is called beriah and is not nullified; but "an egg that has an embryo in it" that was in the egg — mixture cannot be conceived, for if other eggs also have embryos, all are forbidden, and if not, what mixture applies — and this question was already printed in my name in Be'er Heitev and there is no dawn.
1#ד: Even in a thousand — see Peleti to strengthen the view of those who say beriah is nullified in a thousand — see there.
1#ה: And gid hanasheh, etc. — all these have life that comes from life, to exclude grain.
1#ו: Forbidden from the beginning of its creation, etc.
1#ז: And it must be whole, etc.
1#ח: To exclude pure fowl that became nevelah, etc.
2#א: And if there is sixty against its fat — Shach wrote: this is issur davuk — I do not know; since every taste of issur davuk sometimes in a dish without sixty — and in d'rabbanan issur how can we be concerned — it is a d'rabbanan doubt and lenient; especially in gid fat that many were not stringent at all.
2#ב: And if it melted, etc. — see what Peleti wrote in the name of Machatzit HaShekel; and there is proof, for all their proof from R' Nachman gid in sixty and R' Nachman — according to halachah there is no nosen taam in gidim and therefore it refers to gid fat — end of his words.
4#_: Three worms — Taz wrote: in Torah matters two times is chazakah; otherwise three; and Torah niddah blood with veset d'rabbanan requires three — likewise here.
